challenge.better_approach: Sourcing bootstrap.sh and calling cairn_python, as 12 bin/cmd scripts do, is fewer lines, but bin/ is under no component and the gate is a tool: sourcing a device's script reaches past recovery's declared interface (public_interface names only cairn_wire_instances). Widening recovery's interface writes another component's charter. A hand fix on yoga (install the venv) is ruled out by the orchestrator, and it would leave the gate's bare python3 to fail on the next box. Carrying the resolution order in the gate, cited, is the smallest change that holds.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That the compile needs only the standard library plus the repo on its path, so a host Python 3 with no venv compiles it. Measured 2026-11-16 here: under a PATH whose python3 is a stub and python is the host 3.x, cairn_python answers python. And that yoga's FAILED line is the stub's, which the orchestrator relayed; I reproduced the same line with a stub locally.
challenge.prior_art: cairn_python and _cairn_host_python in cairn/devices/recovery/bootstrap.sh (the order, and the probe that skips a stub by running it); 271146bf067d (a runner drive names sys.executable, never a bare PATH name, for the same stub); 337dcf060614 (a bus spawned outside the venv runs the venv's interpreter); 40e40e8e5d53 (skills poke the gate of their own checkout). None covers the gate's interpreter.
challenge.real_collision: None exclusive: f09cd0588ceb's install mode and the never-blocks, loud-in-the-record contract are kept. Distinction recorded: bin/ may source the recovery floor; a tool carries its own copy of the order and cites it.

answers.falsifier: Done when, with no venv and a PATH whose python3 is a stub that exits 9009, the gate writes the lab and logs no FAILED; with a venv present, the gate runs the venv's interpreter; with no interpreter that runs, it exits 0 and logs FAILED naming that none was found. Wrong intent if the Windows boxes need the venv itself rather than any working Python 3 for the compile (then the fix is laying the venv on yoga, not the gate's resolver).
answers.how: Replace the bare python3 in recompile_gate.sh with a resolver carried in the gate itself, in the order of cairn/devices/recovery/bootstrap.sh's cairn_python (cited, not sourced: recovery publishes only cairn_wire_instances, and a tool that sources a device's script reaches past its interface, RULE 1). When no interpreter runs, the gate still exits 0 and records FAILED naming that none was found (Law 7). Red-first proof in cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/proofs runs the gate under a PATH whose python3 is a stub.
answers.shape: aside — a host fix to the post-merge recompile gate f09cd0588ceb laid
answers.traces_to: Law 7 (an error is permanent in the record; here every post-merge poke on akienyoga9i records the same FAILED, and the lab never regenerates) and Law 1 (the lab is what /intent consults, so a lab that never recompiles makes the next mind re-derive the settled).
answers.what: recompile_gate.sh runs the lab compile with the box's cairn interpreter, resolved in the order bin/ resolves it: the venv's bin/python3, then its Scripts/python.exe, then the first of python3, python, py that actually runs Python 3. A stub python3 never runs the compile.

bullets.text: Reproduced on this box: recompile_gate.sh under a PATH whose python3 is a stub exits 0, logs 'recompile-gate FAILED: Python was not found…', and writes 0 lab files; bootstrap.sh's cairn_python in the same world answers python
